clue.text: Face Thomas outside hospital, a shadowy figure

indicators.note: the face word sits outside, wrapping round the hospital letter

parts.note: pan is slang for the face
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
Tom is the short form of the name Thomas

explanation.surface: Someone confronting a man called Thomas outside a hospital, as if meeting a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' reads as a verb, but it is PAN, slang for the face, which goes 'outside' H.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is a ghost or apparition, the very model of an insubstantial, shadowy figure.

clue.text: Easter's hour off for French philosopher

indicators.note: the hour letter goes off, taken out of the Easter word

parts.note: paschal means relating to Easter

explanation.surface: A French thinker takes an hour off at Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaise Pascal was a seventeenth-century French thinker and mathematician.

clue.text: Plant with minimal nitrogen gets behind

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like flowering plant

indicators.note: only the smallest part, the first letter, of the gas is taken

explanation.surface: A plant given little nitrogen falls behind in growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical term for at or towards the back of a ship, so behind.

clue.text: Brawlers using language about a good worker

indicators.note: the language word goes about the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: terms are words or language, as in 'in no uncertain terms'
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: Quarrellers using strong words about a decent employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a violent, quarrelsome, overbearing person, so termagants are brawlers.

clue.text: Symbols offered by man with manifesto in speech

indicators.note: spoken, the philosopher's name matches the answer

parts.note: Karl Marx co-wrote The Communist Manifesto

explanation.surface: A political leader offers slogans and emblems while giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks are signs or symbols, such as punctuation marks.

clue.text: Boy knocked over told fibs and dawdled

indicators.note: something knocked over is turned upside down, so the boy word is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
to tell fibs is to have lied

explanation.surface: A boy was knocked over, lied about it and took his time.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to loiter or waste time, so having dallied is a synonym for having dawdled.

clue.text: After month was first to admit intention and gave a talk

indicators.note: the rest follows the month word

parts.note: Dec is short for December

indicators.note: the leading word lets in the intention word

parts.note: to have led is to have been in front
an aim is an intention

explanation.surface: After a month in the lead, someone admitted their aims in a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the month first; 'to admit' means the leading word takes in the intention, giving LAIMED. 'was first' is a past-tense verb phrase, so its synonym is also past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to speak rhetorically, as in delivering a speech or oration.

clue.text: Set left needing succour

parts.note: aid is help, or succour

explanation.surface: Someone left behind and in need of help.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid and set both mean placed or put down, as with a table laid or set for dinner.

clue.text: Somehow you go idle abandoning university beliefs

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are reassembled in some way
the university letter is left out of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Idling students drop out of university and give up their convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove U from YOU GO IDLE and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideology is a system of ideas and ideals, a body of beliefs.

clue.text: Dislike endless calamity — trembling's beginning inside

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the shortened calamity
the final letter of the calamity word is dropped

parts.note: a disaster is a calamity

indicators.note: the start of the trembling word is used

explanation.surface: Revulsion at a disaster that sets one shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last R of the calamity, leaving DISASTE; 'inside' sets the opening T of trembling within it, after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is aversion or dislike for something.

clue.text: Celebrity one's brought in as music-maker

indicators.note: the one letter is brought into the middle of the celebrity word

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A celebrity is hired to provide the music.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitar is an Indian stringed instrument, and any instrument is a maker of music.

clue.text: Criminals? They get signals coming in

definitions.meaning: people who handle stolen goods, a crime in itself
radios and television sets that pick up broadcast signals

explanation.surface: Wondering whether criminals have a radio link.
explanation.definitionFit: Receivers are both handlers of stolen goods and radio sets that pick up transmissions.

clue.text: Look — Henry is circling planet! A high-flyer in both senses!

indicators.note: Henry is pictured orbiting the planet, so his letters come beside it, just after

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of confidence
Mars is a planet
Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: An exclamation at Henry orbiting a planet, like an astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is circling' places HAL alongside MARS, as a moon orbits close by, rather than wrapping it.
explanation.definitionFit: An air marshal is a senior RAF officer: high in rank and a flyer of aircraft, hence a high-flyer twice over.

clue.text: Excuse of little creature quiet rather than loud

indicators.note: the quiet letter takes the place of the loud letter

parts.note: a flea is a tiny insect
F is forte, the musical direction for loud
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An excuse given by a small creature that kept quiet instead of being noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rather than' swaps P for F in FLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an excuse or appeal offered in one's defence.

clue.text: Funny dames still award-winners

indicators.note: something funny is odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Comic actresses still collecting prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' signals an anagram of DAMES STILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Medallists are people who have won medals, the award of a competition.

clue.text: How one might categorise fighter that's knocked out mate with bang

indicators.note: the letters are knocked out of shape and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A boxer who has flattened his opponent with one blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' reads as boxing, but it signals an anagram of MATE WITH BANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantamweight is a boxing weight division, a category into which a fighter is placed.

clue.text: To entertain party-goers old rocker went across

indicators.note: the rocker word holds the party word, as a host entertains guests

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s youth devoted to rock and roll
ravers are people who go to wild parties

explanation.surface: An ageing rock fan crossed the room to entertain partygoers.
explanation.walkthrough: TEDs were British 1950s Teddy boys, noted for their love of rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across, so traversed means crossed over.

clue.text: Beholden to have mixture of gruel and fat

indicators.note: the two words are mixed together into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Obliged to eat a blend of gruel and fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture of' signals an anagram of GRUEL and FAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beholden is to be indebted or thankful to someone.

clue.text: Corresponding, wasting little time offering a welcome

indicators.note: the time letter is wasted, removed from the phrase

parts.note: a greeting is a welcome
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Offering a quick greeting without spending much time.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that agree correspond or match each other, as in figures that agree.

clue.text: Trusted assistant not inclined to be sinister

definitions.meaning: a most reliable helper or deputy
sinister is Latin for left, so this is a person who favours the right hand

explanation.surface: A loyal helper who has no tendency towards wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is a chief aide; read literally it is someone right-handed, not left, or sinister.

clue.text: Main element in piece of wire

definitions.meaning: the bent wire fastener that binds papers together

explanation.surface: The key component inside a bit of wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is both a basic, principal item and a small U-shaped wire fastener.

clue.text: Actually at home, female needs to do something

parts.note: in means at home
to act is to do something, to take action

explanation.surface: A woman at home really must do something.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an adverbial synonym meaning really, or as a matter of truth.

clue.text: Maybe watch heartless row

indicators.note: the heart, the central letter, is removed from the timepiece word

parts.note: a watch is one example of a timer

explanation.surface: Perhaps a watch reveals an unfeeling quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle M out of TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level, as in the tiers of seating in a stadium.

clue.text: When ill, eat no plain chocolate

indicators.note: being ill puts the letters out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid plain chocolate when you are sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' signals an anagram of EAT NO PLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Neapolitans are small, individually wrapped squares of chocolate, so the word names a kind of chocolate.

clue.text: Word to identify journalist in crowd

definitions.meaning: reporters collectively are the media, a label on a reporter's pass
to crowd or throng is to push in on

explanation.surface: A label that singles out a reporter in a throng.
explanation.definitionFit: Press is the collective term for journalists and also a verb meaning to crowd or throng round.

clue.text: A thousand paintings maybe in business area

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
paintings are an example of art

explanation.surface: A thousand pictures for sale in a commercial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A mart is a market or trading centre, a place where business is done.

clue.text: One day of the week, when to look to eat cold stew

indicators.note: the day and the following words take in the cold letter, as if eating it

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to see is to look
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Choosing a day of the week for eating a cold stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts C inside FRIASSEE, just after FRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A fricassee is a dish of meat cut up and stewed in a thick white sauce.

clue.text: Brownish ape is on the move

indicators.note: letters on the move shift into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A brownish ape is travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' signals an anagram of APE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown tint, as in old photographs, so it describes something brownish.

clue.text: At the end of day Edward rested

indicators.note: the name is placed at the end of the day word

parts.note: daylight, or light, is the daytime as opposed to night
Ed is the short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward put his feet up when the day was done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end of day' looks like a time phrase, but 'At the end of' is a placement signal and 'day' alone is the daylight word.
explanation.definitionFit: To light on something is to alight or settle on it, so lighted means came to rest.

clue.text: Have a feeling one may be spotted in sort of parade

definitions.meaning: to sense or have a hunch

definitions.text: one may be spotted in sort of parade
definitions.meaning: an identity parade, where a witness tries to pick out the person the police believe guilty

explanation.surface: A hunch about someone recognised in a police line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspect as a verb is to have an inkling; as a noun it is the person a witness picks out in an identity parade.
